what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from Haiti in all host countries combined: people who have asked for protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 236318 Haitian asylum seekers, and the United States hosts the largest share, 63.9%.
Mexico and Canada are the next largest hosts.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of Haiti with Viv Ansanm in 2024 and 2025, at war level in 2025.
It records an earlier armed conflict over the government in 2004, with FLRN and OP Lavalas.

when.text: The number of Haitian asylum seekers rose from 19735 in 2000 to a peak of 275050 in 2024.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2022 to 2025; the figure also changed sharply in several earlier years from 2011 to 2021.

how.text: These are year-end totals of people whose claims had not yet been decided; refugees from Haiti are counted in a separate series.
People displaced inside Haiti are counted separately by UNHCR and by IDMC, and their figures are never added.
The sources don't say which routes people took.
